'''Anthony Aguirre''' (born 1973) is an American theoretical [[cosmologist]].<ref name="bio">{{Cite web|url=https://www.anthony-aguirre.com/|title=Anthony Aguirre|website=Anthony Aguirre|accessdate=17 August 2023}}</ref> Aguirre is an adjunct professor of physics at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]].<ref name="stephens">{{cite web|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2016/09/aguirre-appointment.html|title=Physicist Anthony Aguirre appointed to endowed chair in physics of information|date=28 September 2016|access-date=12 September 2020|website=UC Santa Cruz|last=Stephens|first=Tim}}</ref> He is the co-founder and CEO of the [[Future of Life Institute]].<ref name="fqxi_who_page">{{cite web |url=http://fqxi.org/who |title=Who we are |publisher=Foundational Questions Institute |accessdate=25 Nov 2014}}</ref> He is also the co-founder and president of the [[Foundational Questions Institute]].<ref name="fli_who_page">{{cite web |url=http://futureoflife.org/who |title=Who we are |publisher=Future of Life Institute |accessdate=25 Nov 2014}}</ref><ref name="bostinno_elon_article">{{cite web |url=http://bostinno.streetwise.co/2015/01/15/elon-musk-future-of-life-institute-artificial-intelligence-research-could-be-crucial/ |title=3 Things to Know About the Elon Musk-Backed Future of Life Institute|publisher=Bostinno |accessdate= 5 Jun March 2016|date=15 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="engadget_elon_article">{{cite web |url=https://www.engadget.com/2015/01/15/elon-musk-ai-donation/ |title=Elon Musk donates $10M to keep AI from going == Early life and education ==
Aguirre was born on July 23, 1973.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scipp.ucsc.edu/~aguirre/Scipp/Home_files/cv_081308.pdf|title=Anthony N. Aguirre CV|website=ucsc.edu|access-date=17 August 2023}}</ref> He received a B.S. in Mathematics/Physics from [[Brown University]] in 1995, an M.S. in Astronomy from [[Harvard University]] in 1998 and a Ph.D. in Astronomy from Harvard University.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stephens" />

== Career ==
His research has focused on various topics in [[theoretical physics]], including the [[early universe]], [[Cosmic inflation|inflation]], the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]], foundations of [[statistical mechanics]], [[gravity|gravitational]] physics, [[list of oldest stars|first stars]], the [[intergalactic medium]], [[galaxy formation]], and [[Black hole|black holes]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anthony Aguirre |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=2xHWUiAAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

Together with [[Max Tegmark]] he developed the [[cosmological interpretation of quantum mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Aguirre |first=Anthony |last2=Tegmark |first2=Max Erik |date=August 2010 |title=Born in an Infinite Universe: a Cosmological Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics |journal=Physical Review |arxiv=1008.1066}}</ref>

On March 5, 2025, Aguirre published ''Keep The Future Human: Why and How We Should Close the Gates to AGI and Superintelligence, and What We Should Build Instead'', an extended essay that proposes a scheme for the international [[regulation of artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aguirre |first=Anthony |date=5 March 2025 |title=Keep The Future Human: Why and How We Should Close the Gates to AGI and Superintelligence, and What We Should Build Instead |url=https://keepthefuturehuman.ai/essay/ |doi=10.2139/SSRN.4608505 |ssrn=4608505 |accessdate=7 March 2025}}</ref> On November 6, 2025, he published another extended essay, "Control Inversion", arguing that artificial superintelligence would be "fundamentally uncontrollable" by humans.<ref>{{cite web |title=Control Inversion |website= Control Inversion |date=2025-11-06 |url=https://control-inversion.ai/ |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pedrielli |first=Samuel |title=&quot;Control Inversion&quot; Study by FLI: Superintelligence Risks Humanity |website=LinkedIn |date=2025-11-13 |url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/future-of-life-institute_control-inversion-fast-facts-activity-7394782192813584384-S2Yb |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>

== In the media ==
*Aguirre appears in the ''How Vast is the Cosmos?'' part of the ''[[Closer to Truth]]'' [[PBS]] series.
*Aguirre appears on the show ''[[Horizon (British TV series)|Horizon]]'', in the episode "How Big is the Universe?"<ref>{{cite episode |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01mgllj|series-link=Horizon (British TV series)|series=Horizon|network=[[BBC Two]]|number=4|season=[[List of Horizon episodes#Series 49: 2012–2013|49]]|title=How Big is the Universe?|access-date=12 September 2020|date=27 August 2012}}</ref>
*Aguirre also appears in the episode "Living in a Parallel Universe" of the ''[[Naked Science]]'' documentary series on the [[National Geographic Channel]].<ref>{{cite episode |url=https://imdb.com/title/tt1940819/| title=Living in a Parallel Universe|series=Naked Science|series-link=Naked Science|network=National Geographic Channel|season=[[List of Naked Science episodes#Season 8|8]]|number=9|date=19 May 2011|access-date=12 September 2020}}</ref>
*Aguirre was a guest on [[Sean M. Carroll]]’s ''Mindscape'' podcast, which was released on June 17, 2019 under the title of "Cosmology, Zen, Entropy, and Information".<ref>{{cite web |title=Episode 51: Anthony Aguirre on Cosmology, Zen, Entropy, and Information |website=Sean Carroll – Preposterous Universe |date=2019-06-17 |url=https://www.preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/2019/06/17/episode-51-anthony-aguirre-on-cosmology-zen-entropy-and-information/ |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*Aguirre was interviewed in the season 4 of ''[[Through the Wormhole#Season 4|Through the Wormhole]]'', episode 3 ("Can We Survive the Death of the Sun?")<ref>{{cite web |title=Can We Survive the Death of the Sun? |website=Through the Wormhole |date=2026-05-21 |url=https://www.dailymotion.com/video/x9n8wjk |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*In 2022, Aguirre appeared in the [[Netflix]] documentary ''[[A Trip to Infinity]]'',<ref>{{Citation |last1=Halperin |first1=Jonathan |title=A Trip to Infinity |date=2022-09-26 |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt21929356/ |type=Documentary |publisher=Makemake, Room 608 |access-date=8 November 2023|last2=Takahashi |first2=Drew}}</ref> discussing the mathematical implications of [[infinity]].
*In 2022, Aguirre participated as a panelist at the Nobel Week Dialogue in [[Stockholm]], organized by the [[Nobel Prize]] Foundation, where he took part in discussions entitled "Futurism & Utopian/Dystopian Visions" and "Living with Technology" alongside Nobel laureates, including [[Serge Haroche]] and [[Stuart J. Russell]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Futurism and utopian/dystopian visions. The future of life |website=Nobel Prize Foundation |date=2024-03-06 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6NOZ6y-qCrI |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Living with technology. The future of life |website=Nobel Prize Foundation |date=2024-03-06 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2zSKm5uTqwI |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*In 2025 Aguirre participated in an episode of the Big Technology Podcast hosted by Alex Kantrowitz, where he discussed whether our push toward increasingly autonomous, general systems puts control out of reach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Big Technology Podcast Episodes |website=Alex Kantrowitz |date=2024-03-06 |url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLADd6sStSis77HKfbf4KCY6SvthfxeUgn |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*In 2025, Aguirre appeared at Axios House at [[SXSW]] in [[Austin, Texas]], in a "View From the Top" conversation with ''[[Axios (website)|Axios]]'' publisher Nicholas Johnston, where he discussed FLI's campaign to halt the development of AGI and his essay "Keep the Future Human."<ref>{{cite web |title=Axios House SXSW: View From the Top conversation with Future of Life Institute |website=Axios |date=2024-03-06 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MZhGV54xLDg |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*In 2025, Aguirre was interviewed on the For Humanity: An AI Risk Podcast in an episode titled "Keep the Future Human," where he discussed his four essential measures for ensuring a human-centered AI future and FLI's strategy for spending its resources.<ref>{{cite web |title=For Humanity: An AI Risk Podcast |website=For Humanity |date=2024-03-06 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PayBks0FBpw |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*In 2025, Aguirre participated in the Tech & AI Forum at UNGA80 organized by ''[[Foreign Policy (magazine)|Foreign Policy]]'' in New York City, where he took part in a panel called "Safeguarding the Future: Coordinated Approaches to Global AI Policy", alongside international policymakers and technology leaders.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Masin |title=Tech & AI Forum at UNGA80 |website=Foreign Policy |date=2025-07-29 |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/events/fp-unga80/tech-ai-forum-at-unga80/ |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
*In 2026, Aguirre appeared at [[SXSW]] in [[Austin, Texas]], in a fireside chat with tech ethicist [[Tristan Harris]] called "How We Could Lose Control: Avoiding the Paths to Runaway AI," where they discussed the real mechanisms by which humanity could be sidelined by its own AI creations.<ref>{{cite web |title=How We Could Lose Control: Avoiding the Paths to Runaway AI |website=SXSW 2026 Schedule |url=https://schedule.sxsw.com/events/PP1162234 |access-date=2026-05-21}}</ref>
